candidates.title: Browser task recorder for repeatable workflows

ease.reason: README lists browser recording and script export; a small single-site prototype is approachable.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: repeat-task teams might pay; the README lists use cases but shows no demand or payment.

feasibility.reason: A single-site recorder/replayer is plausible, but browser control, selectors, screenshots, and replay failures limit a two-week build.

autonomy.reason: Prepared workflows replay steps; people record tasks, select targets, and handle missed selectors or site changes.

evidence.reason: README details outputs and use cases; real customer use is not established.

candidates.reason: Retained as a researched candidate; after correcting the unsupported scores to evidence-supported maxima, it remains below the publish threshold.

candidates.title: Suta UI design skill

ease.reason: README offers install instructions and 56 patterns; a small skill can start with a few patterns.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: developers may pay for better generated interfaces; demand is unproved.

feasibility.reason: A two-week skill can encode a few patterns; results depend on model and prompt.

autonomy.reason: The agent can select patterns and report static issues; people still review visual quality.

evidence.reason: README includes live demo and one comparison; it says results vary and took longer.

candidates.reason: README documents install paths, 56 patterns, a live demo, and one same-request comparison whose results vary.

candidates.title: Agent generated brand-matched diagrams

ease.reason: The README documents installation and file output, but a compatible skill host and HTML/SVG authoring still take technical setup.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: teams may pay for faster branded diagrams; demand is unproved.

feasibility.reason: A few static templates fit a small two-week experiment; host integration and checking rendered diagrams remain work.

autonomy.reason: Agent drafts diagrams from requests; a person must check correctness and visual quality.

evidence.reason: README documents workflow and output format; it does not establish customer use.

candidates.reason: Retained as a researched candidate; corrected supported scores leave it below the publish threshold.

candidates.title: Browser based handwritten PDF notes

ease.reason: README describes a working browser app; reproducing pressure-sensitive ink adds complexity.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: students might pay for note tools; demand is unproved.

feasibility.reason: A two-week version is limited by drawing, PDF handling, and offline storage details.

autonomy.reason: Saving can be automatic, but note taking and organization remain user work.

evidence.reason: README details features and offline behavior; customer evidence is absent.

candidates.reason: README describes a live open-source browser app and local storage; business model and paid demand are absent.

candidates.title: Human question gate for AI pull requests

ease.reason: README gives a simple copy-in guide, accessible to a beginner.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: maintainers may pay to reduce review burden; demand is unproved.

feasibility.reason: A two-week version is easy to distribute but cannot enforce compliance.

autonomy.reason: The workflow asks a human to answer before generation; it cannot autonomously gate PRs.

evidence.reason: README documents a real example and explicitly says effects are unmeasured.

candidates.reason: README says it is a copied contribution guide, not an enforced blocker, and post-adoption results are unmeasured.

candidates.title: Safari animated WebP player

ease.reason: README gives build steps, but requires a Mac and Xcode 26.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: Safari users may pay for playback support; demand is unproved.

feasibility.reason: Native Safari extension, signing, and iOS/macOS support exceed a small beginner scope.

autonomy.reason: Playback runs in browser after setup; installation and compatibility remain user-dependent.

evidence.reason: README documents implementation and install process, not adoption.

candidates.reason: README says app-store release is unavailable and building requires a Mac with Xcode 26 plus platform signing.

candidates.title: Self hosted model serving cluster

ease.reason: README provides runnable deployment commands, but assumes container/model familiarity.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: developers may pay for local model serving; demand is unproved.

feasibility.reason: A useful model cluster needs hardware, deployment, and performance work beyond two weeks.

autonomy.reason: Serving can continue after deployment; setup, model choice, and operations need people.

evidence.reason: README includes quick starts and a claimed conformance score; independent check is needed.

candidates.reason: README shows Docker and native deployment paths but requires model-serving and hardware setup beyond a modest beginner scope.

candidates.title: Local reverse engineering toolkit

ease.reason: README provides a quick start but targets reverse engineering across complex formats.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: developers may pay for analysis tools; demand is unproved.

feasibility.reason: Binary, native app, and runtime analysis are too specialized for a useful beginner clone.

autonomy.reason: Tools can automate inspection steps, but expert interpretation is essential.

evidence.reason: README describes capabilities and install path, without verified customer evidence.

candidates.reason: README describes binary and application analysis tools; specialist systems knowledge and legal boundaries make a beginner clone unsuitable.
